// R2's receiver used to be matched by spelling against every checker the
// enclosing function declares, so an inner block that takes the name over for
// something else was reported as a quicktest subtest and a repository-wide gate
// refused correct code. The receiver is resolved where it is written instead.
package fixture

import (
	"testing"

	qt "github.com/frankban/quicktest"
)

// runner has nothing to do with quicktest, and its Run takes a callback of its
// own.
type runner struct{}

func (runner) Run(name string, step func(int)) {}

func TestShadowedReceiverIsNotAChecker(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)
	c.Check(1, qt.Equals, 1)

	{
		c := runner{}
		c.Run("an inner c that is not the checker", func(int) {})
	}
}

// The same spelling in the same file, where it really is the checker. Without
// this the fixture would be satisfied by a rule that reports nothing at all.
func TestTheCheckerItselfIsStillReported(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)

	c.Run("a real checker subtest", func(c *qt.C) {
		c.Assert(2, qt.Equals, 2)
	})
}
